text:
Alex G: kicking off a soak in staging to validate per-org quotas + fractional token refill behavior. seeing weird 429 patterns when burst regen is high fractionally. anyone on?
Maya R: on it — what config did you run?
Alex G: used the same harness as last week but bumped client parallelism to 1200 and used a refill_rate=5.5 in the token bucket to mimic uneven traffic.
Kevin L: fractional refill_rate? that might interact poorly with our integer-only stored_tokens math. we had a bug where we floor() intermediate tokens on refill tick.
Sam T: confirmed, telemetry shows regen spikes but the enforcement layer truncates to int which causes transient underflow for short bursts.
Li H: also saw a backlog in the routing queue — requests held while key-level quota check hotpath waits on redis. might amplify 429s during short spikes.
Maya R: repro snippet I used:```yaml
rate_limit:
  scope: per-key
  capacity: 100
  refill_rate: 5.5   # tokens/sec (fractional)
  burst_window_ms: 1000
```
Kevin L: our token bucket implementation expects tokens to be a float, but we persisted tokens in a Redis hash as integer for space reasons. we added a quick cast somewhere.
Alex G: ok that explains the 429 clustering. would prefer either a) keep float tokens in redis b) quantize refill to integer per-second or c) change harness to use integer refill. thoughts?
Sam T: proposal: change enforcement to keep a 'nano-tokens' int (multiply by 1000) to avoid floats in redis and preserve precision. then add a migration that backfills existing keys lazily.
Li H: sounds reasonable. risk is storage blowup but should be negligible with sharded keys. also update dashboard metrics to expose "token_granularity" and "token_fraction_drops".
Maya R: for the immediate soak, I'm going to flip the client to integer refill (5) and re-run so we can distinguish queue/regeneration vs implementation truncation.
SRE Bot: deploy v2-ratefix started by @Kevin L — rollout 10% -> 50% -> 100% with 5m pause.
Kevin L: I'll instrument a histogram on time_wait_on_quota_ms and add a metric for redis_write_size so we can see nano-token overhead if we go that route.
Alex G: also want a dashboard panel that shows per-key 429 spike heatmap over 1m windows + the current bucket tokens. that helped last time.
Sam T: for load generation, we should vary client clock skew and burst shapes: steady, sawtooth, poisson, and microbursts (100ms bursts). current harness supports poisson + sawtooth, will add microburst mode.
Li H: don't forget rollout UX — Console should surface "enforcement mode" (strict/lenient) per org so SREs can toggle lenient during soak. can we wire that to the canary config?
Maya R: we already have a per-org flag in the control plane; just need a console toggle that calls /orgs/{id}/settings. New UX task if we want a one-click "lenient soak" flag.
Kevin L: re: tests — run 3 iterations: integer-refill, float-nano-token prod patch, and queue-optimized (redis pipelined checks). collect metrics: 429-rate, p95 latency, tokens_persisted_size.
Alex G: timeline: Maya re-run integer now (~2h), Kevin will push nano-token branch after quick perf run (~4h), Sam will prepare microburst harness by EOD.
Maya R: re-run started. ETA ~18m for current job. posting logs to the thread when done.
SRE Bot: staging-job-8812 completed: 200k requests, 429 rate 0.9% (previously 5.4%). job logs: https://ci.internal/runs/8812
Alex G: nice. can someone pull the telemetry for the 429 window and attach a screenshot of the heatmap?
Kevin L: grabbing metrics now. preliminary: redis write size up 12% if we use nano-tokens, but 429 rate drops to 0.2% in high-parallel tests.
Li H: let's document the tradeoffs in the ops runbook: storage impact, migration plan, dashboard queries, and rollover handling for expired keys.
Sam T: also add a regression alert in Console: if per-key 429 rate increases >1% vs baseline for 5m, auto-create an incident page with suggested mitigations.
Maya R: job finished and attached logs. looks much smoother with integer refill — but that's an artificial constraint, long-term nano-token seems like the correct fix.
Alex G: agreed. next steps: Kevin opens PR for nano-token storage + migration, Li updates runbook & dashboard panels, Sam adds microburst harness config and alert, Maya wires temporary console toggle for lenient soak. I'll track in a short rollout plan. :thumbsup:
Kevin L: will tag PR with the perf numbers and add a feature flag behind canary.
Li H: I'll draft the dashboard query and add a panel to the "Quotas" dashboard.
SRE Bot: follow-up checklist created: https://tickets.internal/RED-3421
Alex G: thanks all — thread closed for now, keep updates here if any new regressions show up.
